content.title: About
content.content: Toasted bread with potato is a popular snack consisting of a slice of bread topped with a thin layer of boiled potato and toasted until golden. It combines the crisp texture of bread with the soft, slightly sweet flavor of potato.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Toasted bread with potato is often served in cafés and cafeterias as a quick bite.
The tradition of pairing bread and potato dates back to medieval European cuisines where potato was used as a filling for bread.
When properly prepared, the product retains up to 30% of the vitamin C from the potato.
In some regions spices such as rosemary or paprika are added to enhance the taste.
The snack is commonly packaged in single‑serve portions, making it popular in the food‑service industry.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Both bread and potato provide slowly digestible carbs that supply steady energy and help maintain blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Potato, especially when the skin is retained, contributes fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Bread supplies B1, B3 and folate, which are essential for metabolic processes.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The snack provides potassium, magnesium and iron, supporting muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When prepared without added oil, toasted bread with potato remains a low‑fat option.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Bread contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If salt is added to the potato topping, monitor the amount to avoid excessive sodium intake.

items.title: Bacterial growth risk
items.content: When kept at room temperature for more than 2 hours, moisture from the potato can promote bacterial growth.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although not fatty, the carbohydrate load can be high; portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted bread with potato can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, served with sauces such as sour cream or mustard, or used as a base for open‑face sandwiches. Reheat in a toaster or oven to achieve a crisp crust.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the product in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0 °C – +4 °C. For longer storage (more than 5 days) reheat before consumption. Discard if it develops an off‑odor, discoloration, or visible mold.

content.title: About
content.content: Cookie, Peanut Butter, Sugar Free is a crunchy biscuit made with natural peanut butter and sugar substitutes such as stevia or erythritol. It delivers a rich nutty flavor, a subtle sweet aftertaste, and a low glycemic index, making it suitable for people monitoring blood sugar levels.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanut butter contains more monounsaturated fats than most vegetable oils.
Sugar‑free cookies are popular in keto and low‑carb diets.
Non‑caloric sweeteners do not cause cavities and have minimal impact on blood glucose.
Traditional cookies can contain up to 30 % sugar, while this version is virtually sugar‑free.
Peanuts are legumes, not true nuts, but are treated as nuts in culinary contexts.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Peanut butter provides monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The absence of sugar and use of sweeteners prevent sharp spikes in blood glucose.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Peanut butter supplies plant‑based protein that aids tissue repair and satiety.

items.title: Contains vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Low sugar content and the presence of dietary fiber in the dough promote stable digestion.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts are a strong allergen; individuals with peanut allergy should avoid this product.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Peanut butter is calorie‑dense, so portion control is important, especially on weight‑loss plans.

items.title: Sugar‑substitute side effects
items.content: Some sweeteners (e.g., sorbitol) may cause gastrointestinal discomfort when consumed in large amounts.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain recipes add salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The cookie can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to protein shakes, kefir, or yogurt. It pairs well with berries, cottage cheese, and nuts. For a softer texture, briefly warm in the microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation. Discard any cookies with off‑odors or signs of mold.

pork-bacon-smoked-or-cured-reduced-sodiu.title: Pork bacon, smoked or cured, reduced sodium, cooked

content.title: About
content.content: Pork bacon is thinly sliced pork belly that has been smoked or cured and further processed to reduce sodium content. The product is fully cooked and ready to eat without additional heating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional bacon is smoked over wood chips, giving it a distinctive aroma.
Sodium reduction is achieved by replacing part of the salt with milder blends or using osmotic treatment technologies.
Ready‑to‑eat bacon is popular in quick‑prep meals because it has already been thermally processed.
In some countries bacon is classified as a "ready‑to‑eat meat product," simplifying storage requirements.
Smoked bacon can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks after opening.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Bacon provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B12, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Reduced sodium
items.content: Lower salt levels make it a better option for individuals monitoring sodium intake.

items.title: Convenient
items.content: Being ready‑to‑eat saves time in meal preparation.

items.title: High in saturated fat
items.content: Bacon contains saturated fats that, when consumed in excess, may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Presence of nitrates/nitrites
items.content: Some curing methods use nitrite salts, which can be undesirable in large amounts.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to pork or sensitive to certain additives may experience reactions.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Bacon is calorie‑rich, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bacon can be eaten straight from the package, added to salads, sandwiches, pastas, omelets, or used as a flavor enhancer in soups and stews. For a crisp texture, briefly warm it in a skillet.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bacon in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. After opening, consume within 7‑10 days. For longer storage, it can be frozen for up to 3 months.

tea-iced-instant-black-decaffeinated-pre.title: Tea, iced, instant, black, decaffeinated, pre‑sweetened with sugar

content.title: About
content.content: Iced instant black tea, decaffeinated and pre‑sweetened with sugar, is a convenient beverage that prepares quickly by simply adding cold water. It retains the characteristic flavor of black tea while lacking the stimulating effect of caffeine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Instant tea was invented in the early 20th century as a way to brew tea where hot water was scarce.
Decaffeinated black tea is produced by a process that removes most caffeine while preserving flavor compounds.
Pre‑sweetening with sugar makes the drink more appealing to children and those who prefer sweet beverages.
Packaging in single‑serve sachets allows easy portion control.
Iced instant tea is popular at sports events and picnics because of its ease of preparation.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Black tea is rich in polyphenols, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: A caffeine‑free drink contributes to maintaining the body’s water balance.

items.title: Stress reduction
items.content: The lack of caffeine makes it suitable for evening consumption without risking sleep disruption.

items.title: Quick energy boost
items.content: Sugar provides an immediate source of energy, useful during physical activity.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Tannins in black tea can help normalize digestive processes.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Excessive sugar intake may contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of diabetes.

items.title: Tea allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to tea components.

items.title: Decaffeination method
items.content: Some decaffeination processes use chemical solvents; choose products labeled “natural decaffeination” if this is a concern.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Tea can raise stomach acidity, which may be undesirable for individuals with gastritis.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: To prepare, dissolve one sachet (or the indicated amount of dry product) in 200‑250 ml of cold water and stir until fully dissolved. Optionally add a slice of lemon, mint, or ice cubes to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sachets in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, use within 6‑12 months.

yogurt-greek-low-fat-milk-plain.title: Greek Yogurt, Low Fat Milk, Plain

content.title: About
content.content: Greek yogurt made from low‑fat milk is a thick, creamy yogurt with high protein content and low fat. It is produced by straining the whey, which gives it a dense texture and a characteristic tangy flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Greek yogurt typically contains 2–3 times more protein than regular yogurt.
The straining process reduces lactose, making it easier on people with mild lactose intolerance.
Low‑fat versions retain most nutrients while cutting calories.
Greek yogurt is often used as a substitute for sour cream or mayonnaise in recipes.
In many countries it is marketed as a probiotic food because of live cultures.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: A 200 g serving provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The low‑fat version contains less than 0.5 g of fat per serving, suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Yogurt is a good source of calcium for bone health and is often fortified with vitamin D.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Live cultures such as Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium promote gut health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Greek yogurt raises blood sugar slowly, which can help with weight management.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: People allergic to milk proteins (casein) may react to yogurt.

items.title: Lactose content
items.content: Although reduced, some lactose remains, so those with severe intolerance should be cautious.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Some brands add sugar or flavorings; choose plain, unsweetened versions if limiting sugar intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Greek yogurt can be enjoyed on its own, blended into smoothies, used in sauces, dips, baked goods, or as a base for desserts. It pairs well with berries, nuts, honey, and whole‑grain cereals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store yogurt in the refrigerator at 1–4 °C. After opening, consume within 5–7 days and do not leave it at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
